text: Future feature (deferred from 2026-08-16 dark-Stage deliberation on 5D98DBCC): cross-workspace shared read-only serving WITHOUT relaxing workspace containment. The external-path read-sources.yaml design was rejected on NON-NEGOTIABLE Principle III/IV grounds (see docs/decisions/2026-08-16-shared-external-readonly-databases-deliberation.md). Constitution-compliant alternative (Option C): run one graphtor-docs serve process rooted where the shared db legitimately lives and let other dev workspaces consume it as MCP clients. Requires a multiplexing MCP transport (HTTP/SSE or local socket) beyond today's 1:1 STDIO, and structurally eliminates the F6 concurrent-multi-process-file gap. Must carry its own Constitution Check (III + V + authz/exfiltration for the network surface) when planned. Also encompasses truly closing the F6 cross-process read-only ownership/liveness window (deferred from spike 970AE45A). Operator confirmation needed on whether to pursue.

Security hardening (deferred from 2026-08-16 dark-Stage adversarial review of 970AE45A/5D98DBCC): symlink-swap TOCTOU in EngineReadonlyGuard (src/db/store.rs lock:472 / Drop:582). fs::set_permissions follows symlinks and the main db file (index 0) is NOT re-checked with is_reparse_point in lock or Drop (only sidecars index>0 are), relying on the caller's earlier validate_path. Because the guard is held for the DataStore lifetime, an attacker with workspace write access could replace the db file with a symlink to an external target after open; on Drop the guard would chmod that external target. Fix: re-check !is_reparse_point(path) in Drop before restoring permissions and drop the index>0 bypass in lock (verify no regression to the existing exact-permission capture/restore + non-empty-sidecar-preservation tests). Needs its own spike/deliberation as a security-mechanism change (Principle III/IV). Source: Security Reviewer (gemini) P1, corroborated by Correctness Reviewer P3 TOCTOU on clear_stale_readonly_lock.
